variables.meaning: emitted visible primitives and polyline vertices

contract.proof: Canvas2D visits each packed data-space primitive once, projects it through its two retained axis scales, and retains no geometry copy.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every visible primitive has a distinct color and both axes use non-identity ranges.

fullScan.rationale: Rasterizing one invalidated frame must consume every emitted primitive exactly once.

contract.proof: Idempotent disconnect invalidates the owner, cancels its frame and settlement timer, removes stable listeners, disconnects one observer and subscription, releases renderer resources, clears accessible nodes, removes the overlay, and restores borrowed attributes and styles.
contract.adversarialWitness: Disconnect during a pending frame, wheel settlement, active captured pinch, and lost WebGL context leaves zero connection lifecycle diagnostics and ignores stale callbacks.

fullScan.rationale: Cleanup visits only connection-owned resources and bounded accessible nodes.

resources.listeners: 0 or 1 wheel plus 0 or 4 pointer listeners

contract.proof: The adapter filters the bounded projected axis list, dispatches one Chart-owned domain action per enabled axis, retains at most two pointer positions, and replaces one settlement timer. Controller render commands enter the connection's single-frame coalescer.
contract.adversarialWitness: Two-axis pinch plus an enabled wheel burst at a domain limit performs bounded axis lookups, releases pointer capture, leaves browser defaults uncancelled when unchanged, and retains one timer and frame.

fullScan.rationale: Browser input cannot inspect source datums, layers, or unrelated axes.

variables.name: k
variables.meaning: emitted primitives inspected only while interaction state is visible
variables.ceiling: Chart projection representative ceiling; at most 512 overlay markers emitted

contract.proof: The connection-owned SVG samples each axis to at most 512 ticks, emits at most 64 legend entries and 512 interaction markers, and otherwise retains no datum nodes. Interaction marking scans the already bounded emitted batches only when active, cursor, or selection state is visible.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every axis requests the Core tick maximum and the chart declares more than 64 layers.

fullScan.rationale: Overlay work is bounded by resolved axes, sampled ticks, and legend ceilings rather than source datums.

variables.name: s
variables.meaning: polyline spans inspected in those batches

assumptions: This operation covers uniform/attribute setup, not geometry conversion, upload, GPU execution or the renderer's layer registry.
Each named five-value axis tuple is local to a batch. Scalar attribute helpers allocate no arrays or closures.
deterministicWork: A point batch with 1, 1000 or 100000 datums uses one float attribute pointer, two attribute lookups and five vec2 uniform writes.
Disjoint polyline spans use one start/end binding pair per nonempty span; the next point batch resets per-vertex divisors.
contract.resourceRationale: Each axis uses one bounded tuple instead of a record with two child arrays. Only two tuples are live per batch; no axis cache or input-sized temporary is added. Fixed shader text is assembled once per module and shared by renderer instances. GPU resource ownership and rollback remain unchanged.
contract.proof: bindFloatAttribute performs one location lookup, enable, pointer and divisor call using scalar arguments. bindProjection reads five fixed tuple positions per axis. Draw dispatch invokes these helpers once per batch or nonempty line span, never per datum.
contract.adversarialWitness: Linear/log axis combinations, distinct reversed ranges, empty and singleton spans, nonzero vertex/color offsets, retained redraw, large point batches and initialization/restoration failures.

fullScan.rationale: Attribute setup does not inspect datum values; line dispatch only inspects the submitted span offsets.

contract.proof: Each layer owns one geometry buffer and at most one color buffer. Compatible views update uniforms only; changed immutable geometry is converted once and uses a bounded changed-range upload when the calibrated gate admits it.
contract.adversarialWitness: One value changes near each end of a large layer, forcing a full upload, while every unchanged layer retains buffer identity.

fullScan.rationale: A new immutable geometry owner may require one equality-range scan before selecting full versus partial upload; compatible views never inspect its values.

contract.proof: Construction evaluates one selector, retains one record, and inserts it into one form or field Set channel.
contract.adversarialWitness: A subscription to an absent field still allocates one field-channel record and no domain projection.

fullScan.rationale: Subscription construction cannot inspect registered fields or other subscriptions.

variables.name: uSource

variables.name: sAffected

variables.name: sField

contract.proof: Dispatch snapshots the coarse channel and only event-routed field channels; source-wide events reuse Form owner indexes and reset/reinitialize explicitly visit every subscribed field channel.
contract.adversarialWitness: A source replacement touching one of 10k fields evaluates coarse selectors plus only that field's channel, while reset deliberately evaluates every subscribed field channel.

fullScan.rationale: Ordinary single-field updates cannot enumerate unrelated fields or field subscription channels.

contract.proof: The idempotent disposer marks one record inactive, deletes it from one Set, and removes an empty field channel from one Map.
contract.adversarialWitness: Repeated disposal during active dispatch changes no other channel and retains no subscription.

fullScan.rationale: Unsubscribe owns a direct record and channel reference.

assumptions: Canonical Grid position lookup, Map and WeakMap operations have expected constant cost.
Core owns navigation and eligibility semantics; registration projects host state only.
deterministicWork: At 1000, 10000 and 100000 cells, bulk registration writes exactly r roles and r tabIndex values.
Re-registering the same host and disabled value performs zero host writes.
Replacement or identity transfer releases at most two old registrations and projects only the new host.
contract.resourceRationale: Each registration performs expected O(1) work and allocations, so registering r independent hosts takes O(r) total work. The forward Map owns live hosts; the WeakMap maps hosts to primitive stable IDs without retaining detached elements. Release deletes forward/reverse ownership and per-cell disabled state. Disconnect clears strong host ownership and local eligibility state and removes the three root listeners.
contract.proof: setCellAttributes uses canonical positionOf and direct ownership lookups, returns for unchanged registrations, and calls projectCell for one element. Passing undefined releases one registration and its local disabled state. There is no registered-domain traversal in the per-cell operation.
contract.adversarialWitness: Maximum-size registration, numeric 0 versus textual 0, duplicate-host transfer, replacement, disabled toggles, unknown IDs, repeated release, and 32 disconnect cycles with captured callbacks.

fullScan.rationale: One cell registration affects its requested ID and a directly indexed previous owner only.

variables.name: h
variables.meaning: target parentNode ancestry depth up to the listening root

assumptions: Host event target ancestry is acyclic; the existing weak reverse index and forward ownership Map are reused.
The bound describes light-DOM target resolution, separately from Core transitions, focus events and application callbacks.
deterministicWork: Descendant clicks at the last of 1000, 10000 and 100000 registered cells perform zero contains calls.
Traversal reads each visited parentNode at most once; replaced and released hosts have no live forward owner.
contract.resourceRationale: Event routing retains no event target or path and allocates no registry snapshot.
contract.proof: findID follows parentNode, probes the WeakMap and confirms the matching forward Map entry, stopping at the first live host or the listening root. It never enumerates registered cells.
contract.adversarialWitness: Text-like descendants of late-registered cells, numeric/string IDs, detached replacement targets and stale handlers after disconnect.

fullScan.rationale: Only target ancestors participate in event routing.

assumptions: Core Grid selection has at most one selected ID.
The contract covers host attribute projection; canonical transitions, application callbacks, focus dispatch and Vue rendering retain their separate costs.
deterministicWork: An ordinary cursor move writes at most two tabIndex values; a selection change writes at most two aria-selected attributes.
Unchanged state writes nothing and no transition rewrites role, row/column indices or disabled attributes.
All eight controlled ownership shapes project accepted canonical state, including synchronous owner acceptance.
contract.resourceRationale: Only the last projected current and selected IDs are retained. No duplicate domain state or per-transition index is built.
contract.proof: projectTransition compares two stored scalar IDs with the live Core snapshot and directly updates the previous and next hosts of each changed value. Controlled synchronization and focus events use the same projection owner.
contract.adversarialWitness: Maximum domain movement, stopped boundary moves, selection across distant cells, synchronous controlled acceptance, edit callbacks and disconnect with queued focus work.

fullScan.rationale: Current and selected IDs completely identify the affected host state.

variables.name: hPath
variables.meaning: event composed path length, or target ancestor depth for minimal event hosts

resources.allocations: one host-produced composed path; O(1) for the parentNode fallback

assumptions: WeakMap and Map lookups have expected constant cost; the existing element ownership indexes are reused.
This bound covers click target resolution only. Canonical transitions, state projection, and positioning remain separate operations.
ceilings: At most one composedPath call and one traversal prefix ending at the nearest live registered host or the listening root.
deterministicWork: A fixed two-target prefix takes two ownership probes at 1000, 10000, and 100000 registrations, for both unmatched and late-item descendant clicks.
Routing performs zero registered-element contains calls and no full registry traversal.
The forward index confirms live ownership after replacement, unregister, and disconnect; IDs are never string-coerced.
contract.resourceRationale: Only the event's temporary path is materialized; the adapter retains no event, path, new cache, or per-click callback. The minimal-host parentNode walk uses constant auxiliary space.
contract.proof: DOMMenuControl resolves a click through composedPath, or parentNode when the host supplies no path. Each candidate consults the existing reverse WeakMap and verifies its live forward Map entry. The walk stops at the first registered item or the root, never at an unrelated registered ancestor above the root. Core still owns focus, invoke, and submenu transitions.
contract.adversarialWitness: Fixed-depth misses and late-registration descendants across 1k/10k/100k items; exact numeric/textual IDs, replaced/unregistered hosts, nested SVG/text descendants, disabled items, submenu opening, and captured post-disconnect handlers. All four Vue menu roots exercise adopted descendants; Chromium checks open/closed shadow paths and the root boundary.

fullScan.rationale: Only the event ancestor path is relevant to registered target lookup; unrelated menu registrations are not visited.

variables.name: nRegistered
variables.meaning: item elements already registered by this menu connection

assumptions: WeakMap and Map lookup are expected O(1)
the item identity belongs to the canonical menu tree
deterministicWork: one reverse element-owner lookup and bounded map updates
one touched-item attribute projection and no registered-domain sweep
contract.resourceRationale: The existing ID-to-element registry remains the strong owner; the reverse WeakMap adds one non-retaining ownership entry per mounted element and no lifecycle resource.
contract.proof: setItemAttributes resolves duplicate host ownership through one WeakMap lookup, repairs at most the current ID and one prior owner, projects only the newly registered element, updates only its submenu position when present, and retries only pending focus.
contract.adversarialWitness: Sequentially register a maximum flat leaf domain of distinct elements, then transfer one existing element to another ID; projection writes stay constant per registration and replacement never scans prior registrations.

fullScan.rationale: Incremental item registration may touch only the requested ID, a reverse-lookup prior owner, and the newly registered element.

variables.name: s
variables.meaning: live submenu surfaces registered on this connection

assumptions: Map/WeakMap and canonical Tree depth lookup have expected constant cost. Core openPath contains one root-to-branch entry per depth.

This bound covers registry ownership, attribute/visibility projection and affected position selection; platform positioning, DOM focus dispatch and arbitrary consumer callbacks retain their independent costs.
ceilings: Registration touches the requested surface/anchor and at most one indexed prior surface owner, not all registered items or submenus.
An unchanged surface/ID registration performs no host writes or registry enumeration.
deterministicWork: All four DOM menu families register 16/128/1024 branches with zero Map iterator visits, zero root writes, zero unrelated leaf projection and at most five anchor writes per surface.
All four Vue menu families mount 16/64/128 submenu surfaces within a fixed linear branch-projection bound.
contract.resourceRationale: The existing forward Map strongly owns live surfaces; the new reverse WeakMap stores primitive IDs without independently retaining elements. Release removes both directions and existing visibility, ID and positioning resources. No event history or duplicate canonical open-state index is retained.
contract.proof: setSubmenuAttributes probes the reverse index for transfers, then projects one anchor and surface. Open membership is read at the canonical Tree depth instead of scanning the path. Only that branch position is created/updated. Full refresh remains an explicit separate operation. Release uses the existing restoration/disposal paths and deletes the weak reverse entry.
contract.adversarialWitness: Sequential distinct surfaces, unchanged registrations, numeric/string IDs, 32 ownership transfer cycles, late-open registration, sibling isolation, consumer-owned ID/controls overrides, existing positioned replacement/unregister and retained-focus scenarios.

fullScan.rationale: Only directly indexed registration owners and the affected branch projection change.

variables.name: hPath
variables.meaning: combined lengths of the previous and current canonical open paths
variables.ceiling: twice the canonical menu tree depth

assumptions: The canonical tree and host policy configuration are stable between explicit full refreshes or connection replacement.

This bound covers DOM projection and affected position-connection selection. Core transitions, layer management, actual positioning, browser focus dispatch, application callbacks, and Vue rendering retain their separate contracts.
Canonical menu open paths are ancestor chains; differences after their common prefix identify the affected anchors and surfaces.
ceilings: Cursor movement changes at most two registered tabIndex properties. A leaf click performs at most three cursor writes across focus and invocation.
Only changed open-path suffixes update aria-expanded, owned visibility, and position connections; root state updates only when open changes.
deterministicWork: At 1000, 10000, and 100000 flat registrations, next and previous each write two tabIndex values and zero static item attributes; unchanged focus writes none.
Nested transition traces match deliberate full reconciliation while unrelated registered submenus receive no visibility reads or position updates.
All four Vue menu families perform zero part-discovery queries during navigation, invocation, and presence completion; later-mounted parts register through their refs.
contract.resourceRationale: The connection retains its last published immutable Core state, not a second item index or state machine. That reference is replaced on publication and cleared on disconnect. Renderer presence refresh selects only its root or submenu position and pending focus.
contract.proof: Event and controlled-sync publication compare the live canonical state with the last host publication. Cursor lookup is constant; one common-prefix scan plus two suffix loops visit only bounded paths. Explicit refresh retains full host reconciliation for external policy or host changes, while Vue discovers declarative parts only when connecting.
contract.adversarialWitness: Large flat menus, nested branches with 64 unrelated submenu owners, controlled synchronous acceptance and callback ordering, explicit policy refresh, late-mounted Vue items, and the existing Chromium retained-reopen/focus/lifecycle scenarios.

fullScan.rationale: Canonical interaction publication visits changed cursor hosts and open paths; deliberate full host refresh is a separate operation.

contract.proof: Connection discovers the owned ancestor chain once; source-owned WeakMap registries retain one physical listener and only callbacks for connections affected by that source.
contract.adversarialWitness: Deep nested scrolling ancestors with every target connected.

fullScan.rationale: Global documents or unrelated connections must never be scanned.

contract.proof: Cleanup visits each connection-owned disposer once and clears all retained resources.
contract.adversarialWitness: Maximum ancestor registrations followed by repeated idempotent disconnect.

fullScan.rationale: Only the connection-owned disposer vector is visited.

contract.proof: Discovery walks the owned overflow/document ancestor chain once and records each unique source.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every ancestor establishes a distinct clipping or scrolling context.

fullScan.rationale: Initial connection discovery must classify every owned ancestor exactly once.

contract.proof: Generation coalescing retains at most one pending update callback per connection.
contract.adversarialWitness: Many synchronous invalidations before the next frame still retain one scheduled callback.

fullScan.rationale: Scheduling cannot inspect ancestors, candidates, or unrelated connections.

contract.proof: An update consumes retained discovery, completes reference/floating/boundary/ancestor reads, invokes the bounded Core AnchoredLayout solver, then commits one owned projection.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every ancestor clips and every side candidate overflows.

fullScan.rationale: Ordinary updates cannot rediscover ancestors or scan global connections.

variables.name: h
variables.meaning: canonical or fallback header node count

variables.name: qCell
variables.meaning: cell membership and headers-link projection queries

assumptions: Tabular owns the canonical start/center/end column partitions and retains their identity for repeated projection reads over one column state.
Accepted column-schema revisions identify header-topology generations; an equivalent partition identity replacement may be compared once and rebound without rebuilding DOM header state.
ceilings: The retained column index and leaf-header IDs contain at most c entries; retained header metric and element-ID maps contain at most h entries.
contract.resourceRationale: A real projected-column or accepted schema-revision change rebuilds one bounded column/header index. An identity-only equivalent partition replacement performs one O(c) equality pass without rebuilding header state. Stable cell and header projection performs expected O(1) Map lookup work and disconnect clears all retained entries.
contract.proof: The connection consumes Tabular's retained start/center/end partitions directly, builds one columnID-to-index Map, and passes that owner-derived index into the DOM header-metric projection exactly once per real column/schema change. Header metrics, header element IDs, and leaf header IDs are retained by identity. registerCell, setCellAttributes, setHeaderCellAttributes, and refresh then use Map lookups; none reconstruct semantic pin/hide ordering or the complete header domain per element.
contract.adversarialWitness: The production-path regression registers 25, 100, and 200 cells in one accepted row. The first lookup performs exactly c column-index writes and one c-item fallback-header materialization with zero raw scans of the retained semantic column order; one refresh and c header lookups add no rebuild work. A row-only accepted-view replacement with an equivalent partition and schema revision performs zero index/header rebuilds. A real column reorder, after Tabular prepares its semantic partition, and a later schema-revision replacement each rebuild exactly once and remain stable afterward.
deterministicWork: packages/dom/tests/tabular.test.mjs DOM DataTable retains one column and header projection across cell registration and refresh

fullScan.rationale: One current projection/schema identity change may derive the bounded column/header domain once; per-cell and per-header host projection cannot rebuild it.

contract.proof: One logical pin-order index is built for visible columns, then each canonical header node contributes once to a descendant interval and metric.
contract.adversarialWitness: A deep grouped header tree with hidden leaves and all three pin regions produces exact start and span values without any descendant column lookup scan.

fullScan.rationale: Refreshing header attributes projects the current complete canonical header topology once.

variables.name: nRow
variables.meaning: rows in the current accepted DataTable projection

variables.name: qRow
variables.meaning: row-identity queries from row registration, cell registration, and registered-row refresh

assumptions: Accepted Tabular row arrays and row identities are canonical and immutable for their retained view identity.
contract.proof: The DOM DataTable connection builds one Map from row ID to canonical projected row when projection.rows identity changes. Row registration resolves once and passes the resolved row directly to ARIA projection; cell registration and later row refreshes reuse Map.get. Repeated reads over the same accepted rows perform no projected-row array scan, and disconnect clears the index and its retained row references.
contract.adversarialWitness: The DOM Tabular production-path regression uses 100, 500, and 1,000 accepted rows. The first row lookup for each accepted view writes exactly nRow index entries; the remaining row registrations, one full refresh, and one cell registration per row perform zero accepted-row Array.find predicate evaluations and no second index build. Replacing the view while rows remain registered rebuilds exactly one new entry and rejects an old row identity.
deterministicWork: packages/dom/tests/tabular.test.mjs DOM DataTable retains one projected-row index across registration refresh and cell registration

fullScan.rationale: One accepted-view identity change may scan its rows once to build the connection-owned index; ordinary row and cell registration or refresh cannot rescan the projection.

variables.name: n
variables.meaning: previous and native text code-unit count

contract.proof: Reconciliation scans a shared prefix and suffix at most once, emits one Core replace transition, and retains only one active composition record plus one generation-guarded composition finalizer.
contract.adversarialWitness: A 100k-code-unit replacement differing only in the final surrogate pair reconstructs the exact native value within the deterministic two-input-length inspection ceiling; disconnect invalidates the pending finalizer.

fullScan.rationale: Autocomplete, history, and selectionless input types expose the resulting value but not a trustworthy changed range, so exact reconciliation may inspect the complete owned value.

variables.name: rFrame
variables.meaning: registered frame regions plus scrollport and surface

assumptions: every registry and scheduled frame is connection-owned
disconnect is idempotent
deterministicWork: one listener removal and two observer disconnects
all connection-owned registries become empty
a pending frame is cancelled and stale callbacks observe the inactive generation
contract.resourceRationale: Disconnect visits and releases only resources retained by one virtualizer connection.
contract.proof: The connection removes its stable scroll handler, disconnects both observers, cancels one pending frame, and clears each owner-local frame, item, pending-entry, and placement registry exactly once.
contract.adversarialWitness: Disconnect during simultaneous frame and item invalidation, then invoke captured observer and animation-frame callbacks and verify zero publication or resource recreation.

fullScan.rationale: Cleanup may visit only connection-owned registrations and placements.

variables.name: rFrame
variables.meaning: geometry observer entries from the bounded host frame
variables.ceiling: registered frame regions plus scrollport and surface

variables.name: kPlacement
variables.meaning: placements emitted and indexed by the owning layout query

assumptions: portable viewport and correction algebra is delegated to @sectile/virtual
the owning layout query and repair retain their registered package bounds
deterministicWork: at most one scheduled animation frame per connection
one surface-frame read per geometry-invalidated transaction
one measurement batch, at most one correction write and one final query, and one accepted plan publication
a failed post-write query or viewport read adds one restoration write before error reporting and publishes no state or plan
contract.resourceRationale: One connection retains two observers, one scroll listener, one pending frame, registered elements, changed entries, and the current placement index. Scroll settlement adds only constant transaction-local state.
contract.proof: Geometry and item callbacks coalesce into one generation-guarded frame; the transaction resolves only changed entries, composes frame and layout deltas, and performs one correction write and query. A rejected post-write query restores the two saved physical coordinates through the configured writer before error reporting. Accepted frames index each emitted placement once; ordinary uncorrected scroll adds no transaction allocation or geometry read.
contract.adversarialWitness: A header resize and changed mounted items still produce one successful write and query. Repeated mutation, measurement, inset, frame, and target-scroll rejections restore the old scroll/state/plan; custom RTL coordinates, host snapping, reused viewport objects, and throwing error callbacks preserve the same rollback boundary.

fullScan.rationale: The DOM layer may visit only bounded frame entries, changed mounted items, and emitted placements; it cannot scan the logical item domain.

variables.name: kPlacement
variables.meaning: placements emitted and indexed by the owning layout query

assumptions: the cached surface frame is current
the owning layout query retains its registered package bound
deterministicWork: zero getBoundingClientRect calls on ordinary scroll
one physical viewport read and one owning query
one placement-index insertion per emitted placement
contract.resourceRationale: Ordinary scroll reuses the connection frame and replaces only the current emitted placement index.
contract.proof: The stable scroll listener marks the viewport dirty, one coalesced frame reads scalar scroll offsets, projects through the cached frame, delegates one query, and indexes each returned placement once.
contract.adversarialWitness: A maximum-output viewport scrolls without any geometry invalidation and performs zero element rectangle reads.

fullScan.rationale: Ordinary scroll may process emitted placements only, never mounted elements or the full logical domain.
